facts.statement: Epidexipteryx is the earliest known dinosaur genus with ornamental feathers in the fossil record.
facts.quote: Epidexipteryx represents the earliest known example of ornamental feathers in the fossil record.

facts.statement: The species name Epidexipteryx hui honors paleomammologist Hu Yaoming, whose name means "Hu's display feather" in English and "Hu Yaoming's display dragon" in Chinese.
facts.quote: The specific name, Epidexipteryx hui ("Hu's display feather"), and its Chinese name Húshì Yàolóng ("Hu Yaoming's display dragon") were coined in memory of paleomammologist Hu Yaoming.

facts.statement: The formal description of Epidexipteryx was published in the journal Nature on October 23, 2008.
facts.quote: The paper was officially published in the October 23, 2008 issue of the journal Nature.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Epidexipteryx hui measures 25 cm in length and was estimated to weigh 164 grams.
facts.quote: In all, the skeleton of Epidexipteryx hui measures 25 cm in length (44.5 cm including the incomplete tail feathers), and the authors estimated a weight of 164 g, smaller than most other basal avialans.

facts.statement: The fossil includes four long tail feathers composed of a central rachis and vanes.
facts.quote: E. hui is known from a well-preserved partial skeleton that includes four long feathers on the tail, composed of a central rachis and vanes.

facts.statement: The tail feather vanes of Epidexipteryx were made of a single ribbon-like sheet rather than individual branched filaments.
facts.quote: However, unlike in modern-style rectrices (tail feathers), the vanes were not branched into individual filaments but made up of a single ribbon-like sheet.

facts.statement: The skull of Epidexipteryx resembles those of Sapeornis, oviraptorosaurs, and therizinosauroids.
facts.quote: The skull of Epidexipteryx is also unique in a number of features, and bears an overall similarity to the skull of Sapeornis, oviraptorosaurs and, to a lesser extent, therizinosauroids.

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx possessed teeth only in the front of its jaws, with long forward-angled teeth similar to those of Masiakasaurus.
facts.quote: It had teeth only in the front of the jaws, with unusually long front teeth angled forward, a feature only seen in Masiakasaurus among other theropods.

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae of Epidexipteryx resembled the pygostyle found in modern birds and some oviraptorosaurs.
facts.quote: The tail of Epidexipteryx also bore unusual vertebrae towards the tip which resembled the feather-anchoring pygostyle of modern birds and some oviraptorosaurs.

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx had a hip configuration where the pubis was shorter than the ischium, a trait similar to Scansoriopteryx.
facts.quote: The rest of the skeleton bore an overall similarity to the possibly closely related Scansoriopteryx, including a hip configuration unusual among other dinosaurs: the pubis was shorter than the ischium, itself expanded towards the tip.

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx likely lacked wing feathers but may have had a membrane wing for gliding, similar to the related dinosaur Yi.
facts.quote: Epidexipteryx appears to have lacked remiges (wing feathers), though based on the related Yi, it may have possessed some sort of membrane wing to allow gliding.

facts.statement: Researchers have hypothesized that Epidexipteryx used its long claws to dig for grubs in trees, similar to the aye-aye.
facts.quote: In addition it has been compared to an Aye aye using its long claws to rummage through trees in search of grubs to eat.

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx lived in the Middle or Upper Jurassic of Inner Mongolia, China, approximately 160 to 154 million years ago.
facts.quote: Epidexipteryx is known from the Middle Jurassic or Upper Jurassic age Daohugou Beds of Inner Mongolia, China (about 160 or 154 mya).

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic position of Epidexipteryx within the group Paraves remains uncertain.
facts.quote: The exact phylogenetic position of Epidexipteryx within Paraves is uncertain.

facts.statement: A 2024 study by Cau suggests Epidexipteryx may be a junior synonym of Epidendrosaurus due to incomplete fossil evidence and variable traits.
facts.quote: Cau (2024) cast doubt on the validity of Epidexipteryx, considering it a junior synonym of the contemporary Epidendrosaurus due to the diagnosis being based on incomplete tail remains within the holotype, the length of the presacral series, which is not fully known in Epidendrosaurus, and the co-ossification of the 10 distalmost cervical centra, which is interpreted as an ontologically variable trait.

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx hui is the only known species of the extinct maniraptoran theropod genus Epidexipteryx, which lived during the late Jurassic, approximately 160 million years ago in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Epidexipteryx hui es la única especie conocida del género extinto Epidexipteryx de dinosaurio terópodo maniraptor que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 160 millones de años durante el Oxfordiense, lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx hui was a small animal with a skeleton 25 cm long, a total length of 44.5 cm including incomplete tail feathers, and an estimated weight of 164 grams.
facts.quote: En total, el esqueleto de Epidexipteryx hui mide 25 centímetros de largo, 44,5 centímetros incluyendo las plumas de la cola incompletas y los autores estimaron un peso de 164 gramos

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx had teeth only at the front of its jaws, with unusually long front teeth projecting forward.
facts.quote: Tenía dientes solamente en el frente de las mandíbulas, con los dientes delanteros inusualmente largos y proyectados hacia adelante

facts.statement: The skull of Epidexipteryx is unique and resembles the skulls of Sapeornis, oviraptorosaurs, and, to a lesser extent, therizinosauroids.
facts.quote: El cráneo del Epidexipteryx es también único en un número de características, y lleva una semejanza total al cráneo de Sapeornis, ovirraptorosaurianos y, en un grado inferior, tericinosáuridos

facts.statement: The rest of the Epidexipteryx skeleton closely resembles that of Epidendrosaurus, suggesting a close relationship between the two.
facts.quote: El resto del esqueleto posee una semejanza total a Epidendrosaurus con el cual parece estar estrechamente vinculado

facts.statement: The tail of Epidexipteryx has unusual vertebrae at the end that resemble the pygostyle of modern birds and some oviraptorosaurs.
facts.quote: La cola de Epidexipteryx también posee vértebras inusuales hacia el final que se asemeja al pigóstilo de pájaros modernos y de algunos oviraptorosáuridos

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx is known from a well-preserved partial skeleton that includes four long tail feathers composed of a central rachis and barbs.
facts.quote: Se conoce por un esqueleto parcial bien preservado que incluye cuatro plumas largas en la cola, compuesta por un raquis central y barbas

facts.statement: Unlike modern tail feathers, the barbs of Epidexipteryx were not branched into individual filaments but were composed of a single ribbon-like sheet.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, a diferencia de las modernas timoneras, plumas de cola, las barbas no fueron ramificados en filamentos individuales sino fueron compuestos de una sola hoja con forma de cinta

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx preserved a simpler body feather cover made of parallel scales similar to those of more primitive feathered dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Del "Epidexipteryx" también se conservó una cubierta de plumas más simples en el cuerpo, integrada por lengüetas paralelas como la de los dinosaurios emplumados más primitivos

facts.statement: Some body feathers of Epidexipteryx were unique in appearing to have a membranous structure.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, las plumas del cuerpo del Epidexipteryx eran únicas en que algunas parecen presentarse de una "estructura membranosa"

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx represents the oldest known example of ornamental feathers in the fossil record.
facts.quote: Epidexipteryx representa el ejemplo más antiguo conocido de plumas ornamentales en el registro fósil

facts.statement: Despite its close relationship with birds, Epidexipteryx likely lacked wing feathers and could not fly.
facts.quote: A pesar de su relación estrecha con las aves, Epidexipteryx parece haber carecido de remeras o rémiges en las plumas del ala, y no podrían volar probablemente

facts.statement: Zhang et al. suggest that unless Epidexipteryx evolved from flying ancestors that later lost their wings, its advanced display tail feathers may have preceded flight or gliding.
facts.quote: Zhang et al. sugiere que a menos que 'Epidexipteryx se hubiera desarrollado de antepasados voladores y posteriormente perdido sus alas, las plumas avanzadas de la exhibición en la cola pudieron haber precedido al vuelo o al deslizamiento

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Daohugou Formation of Inner Mongolia, dating to approximately 168 to 160 million years ago.
facts.quote: El fósil fue hallado en el Lecho Daohugou de Mongolia Interior que fatal de hacer aproximadamente entre 168 a 160 millones de años

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx was officially described in the journal Nature on October 23, 2008.
facts.quote: Al poco fue correctamente descrito oficialmente en la revista Nature en la edición del 23 de octubre de 2008 de la revista Nature

facts.statement: The specific name Epidexipteryx hui means "Hu's display feather," and its Chinese name Hushi Yaolong means "Hu Yaoming's dragon," honoring paleontologist Hu Yaoming.
facts.quote: El nombre específico, Epidexipteryx hui, que significa "pluma de exhibición de Hu", y su nombre chino Hushi Yaolong, "dragón de Hu Yaoming", se acuñaron en memoria del paleomamólogo Hu Yaoming

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic position of Epidexipteryx within Paraves is uncertain.
facts.quote: La posición filogenética exacta de Epidexipteryx dentro de Paraves es incierta

facts.statement: The authors of its description recovered Epidexipteryx as a member of the family Scansoriopterygidae and as a basal member of the clade Avialae.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético realizado por los autores de su descripción lo recuperó como miembro de la familia Scansoriopterygidae y como miembro basal del clado Avialae

facts.statement: A separate exploratory analysis recovered Scansoriopteryx/Epidendrosaurus as a basal Avialae member unrelated to Epidexipteryx, which remained outside Eumaniraptora.
facts.quote: Un análisis exploratorio separado que incluyó Scansoriopteryx/Epidendrosaurus, que se recuperó como miembro basal de Avialae. Los autores notaron que no estaba relacionado con Epidexipteryx, que permanecía fuera de Eumaniraptora

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx lived during the Callovian stage, from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx belongs to the parent group Paraves.
facts.quote: Parent group: Paraves

facts.statement: Epidexipteryx is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
